output.brief: The rise in VA-220 failures traces to Pellacott's valves built in 2026, not to the new installers or firmware 4.2. Teardowns show a deformed, unseated slide seal. About 11% of never-installed 2026 Pellacott valves leak at the seat, against 1 in 100 for 2025 Pellacott valves and 0 in 100 for Durrant-Hale. Claim rates are the same across installer and firmware groups for Pellacott valves, while Durrant-Hale valves stay low in every group. The leak-test rig was out of service from January 2026, and no VA-220 test program exists on the other rigs. Certificate tables repeat four sequences, some dating from before 2026. So the certificates that lifted Pellacott's score and earned dock-to-stock appear not to reflect real tests. I'm fairly sure of this. Still unknown: whether the seal change or the Line 3 move is the cause, and whether other suppliers' records are also unreliable. Next steps: do not release the six held lots on new certificates. Quarantine 2026-built Pellacott stock and suspend dock-to-stock. Retest with Brenmoor's own helium test. Drop the installer remediation plan and the chargebacks. Require rig logs or witnessed tests for scoring, and spot-check other suppliers. Separate the seal and line effects before choosing a seal fix.
